hypothesis: candidate_pool: PIT SEC 8-K Item 2.05 restructuring-cost events are normally negative, but when signal-day price action absorbs the announcement versus SPY, the cost-reset/overhang-relief information may create a next-open 10-trading-day default-off paper candidate.
causal_components: structured SEC submissions item-code event parser

prediction.confidence_reason: 8-K Item 2.05 is a free PIT SEC submissions field with clearer economics than broad 8-K labels and enough cache coverage, but recent SEC event absorption scouts failed and restructuring announcements may reflect real distress rather than overhang relief.

execution_envelope.liquidity_source: price >= $10 and ADV20 >= $50M from PIT OHLCV
execution_envelope.order_semantics: observe-only next-session-open paper entry; no broker order
execution_envelope.portfolio_displacement: none unless a later shared helper and activation gate pass
execution_envelope.kill_switch: trade_enabled remains false; no production adapter changes
execution_envelope.failure_handling: missing SEC submissions cache, missing CIK mapping, missing 8-K Item 2.05 event rows, missing OHLCV, missing next open, or missing 10d exit rejects the paper candidate

production_impact.parity_note: This experiment changes no production code. A positive result is only a replay lead until a shared default-off helper computes the same PIT SEC 8-K Item 2.05 events, acceptance-time signal date, price-absorption gate, cooldown, next-open paper entry, 10-day exit, costs, and concentration controls in both historical replay and daily production.
